jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Agemark Senior Living | Sacramento, CA | Full-Time

Lead a Community. Change Lives. Build a Legacy.

Agemark Senior Living is looking for a dynamic, hands-on Executive Director to lead one of our senior living communities in Sacramento, CA. We’re looking for a servant leader who knows how to build strong teams, create an exceptional experience for residents and families, and successfully manage the operational and financial health of a community.

This person must have previous Executive Director/Administrator experience

and know the state regulations for Assisted Living in CA

What You'll Do

Lead Our People

Lead by example and stay actively connected to all areas of the community.

Hire, train, coach, and develop a strong team while empowering department leaders to succeed.

Drive employee engagement through communication, recognition, accountability, and development.

Lead daily stand-ups, leadership meetings, and regular staff and safety meetings.

Address performance concerns fairly and foster a positive, supportive workplace culture.

Champion Our Residents

Partner with residents, families, service providers, and staff to provide personalized, consistent care and service.

Help residents live with safety, dignity, and independence.

Work closely with clinical leadership to support care planning, problem resolution, and family communication.

Monitor resident and family satisfaction and champion Agemark's Life Enrichment programming.

Drive Occupancy & Growth

Take ownership of occupancy goals and support sales, marketing, and community outreach efforts.

Partner closely with the sales team to achieve monthly goals and maintain strong occupancy.

Build relationships throughout the Sacramento community and represent Agemark with professionalism and integrity.

Manage the Business

Develop and operate within the annual community budget.

Oversee billing, collections, vendor relationships, and expense management.

Manage staffing and scheduling to control labor costs and overtime.

Set and track community goals while identifying opportunities for continued improvement.

What You Bring

A degree in healthcare, business, nursing, geriatrics, or a related field preferred.

Prior leadership experience in senior living, healthcare, or a related industry required.

At least 2 years of experience managing both staff and a budget.

Strong leadership skills with a track record of integrity, sound judgment, and follow-through.

Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.

Comfort with technology and day-to-day computer systems.

Strong attention to detail and discretion with confidential information.

Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, or holidays as community needs require.

A natural ability to build strong relationships with employees, residents, families, and community partners.

What We Offer

A meaningful leadership role where your work directly impacts residents, families, and employees.

Ownership over people, operations, occupancy, and financial performance.

Regional and corporate support with established systems and resources.

Opportunities to grow professionally and make a lasting impact.

Competitive Compensation And Benefits.

Ready to lead with us?

Apply today and bring your leadership to Agemark Senior Living in Sacramento.

Agemark is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE)

jobs.description:
Salary:
$115,000 to $125,000 DOE

General Statement of Duties:

The Executive Director manages, plans, directs, controls, and supervises housing management and operations, human resources, and financial management of allocated resources, including development, construction, and infrastructure projects. Ensures compliance with all applicable federal, state, and tribal laws, rules, and regulations.

Position Summary:

Provides leadership and direction for the All Mission Indian Housing Authority, an authorized Tribally Designated Housing Entity (TDHE) serving fourteen (14) Indian tribes in Southern California. Responsible for managing, planning, directing, controlling, and supervising human resources, property management, financial management, records management, and maintenance operations. Manages multi-million-dollar projects in accordance with federal and state laws, rules, and regulations. Develops annual budgets, contracts, and grants, including funding agreements. Coordinates, collaborates, and communicates with the Board of Commissioners regarding organizational policies, approval of contracts, and implementation of projects, including infrastructure and community housing development projects such as Low-Income Housing Tax Credit housing developments. Maintains inventory compliance with established policies and procedures, oversees capital asset management, and develops corrective action plans to address identified deficiencies. Establishes and maintains professional relationships with stakeholders and staff to ensure the highest level of service to the communities served.

Job Responsibilities:

Provide strategic vision and leadership for the organization by developing and implementing a comprehensive strategic plan, and by developing and revising strategic goals based on unmet needs and the avoidance of duplication or overlap of resources to ensure long-term organizational sustainability and growth.
Promote collaborative impact and governance and drive the success of a diverse culture.
 Support department and program operations for team members in the delivery of best practices by providing quality services for tribal individuals and families served through the organization and tribal communities.
Promote the mission statement by engaging in and participating in community events, forums, civic organizations, and advocacy, and develop effective partnerships with tribal communities, agencies, and programs on housing assistance opportunities while maintaining strong working relationships with tribal groups.
Ensure policy activities align with the mission and vision of the organization and implement policies established by the Board of Commissioners, recommending new or revised policies as needed.
Serve as the primary spokesperson for the organization to stakeholders, media, and the public.
Develop a financial strategy that complies with funding agencies’ rules and regulations; oversee the organization’s financial budgets, resources, and asset management; administer financial and administrative functions to ensure immediate and long-term fiscal integrity; and manage financial resources allocated for affordable housing development in accordance with applicable laws and budget guidelines.
Develop and submit an annual report and budget for the Board of Commissioners’ review and approval and provide regular updates and operational reports to the Board regarding key decisions, financial matters, program operations, and the utilization of organizational resources.
Maintain contact with appropriate branches of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to ensure compliance with NAHASDA program guidelines and regulations, and oversee the preparation and submission of required financial, regulatory, and performance reports.
Prepare funding applications for grants, including but not limited to ICDBG and IHBG
Interpret and enforce the Authority’s Human Resources Policy; approve personnel actions as described in the policy; conduct performance appraisals of direct-report staff; review performance appraisals prepared by Department Heads and others, as deemed appropriate; establish departmental performance goals; monitor departmental performance; and implement strategies to improve performance.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

Education:

High school diploma required. Minimum of a bachelor’s degree (master’s preferred) in business, public administration, finance, or related fields from an accredited college or university plus five (5) years of executive management experience (or equivalent combination).

Experience:

Knowledge of federal budgets and accounting including 2 CFR Part 200 Uniform Administrative Guidance and HUD Federal housing experience is highly desirable. Possess five (5) years of housing experience managing and administering housing programs, and possesses the ability to build effective teams, ability to negotiate, coordinate several major management functions simultaneously and projects. Possess five (5) years of executive leadership experience in housing management operations and community development including infrastructure project management.

Skills:

Incorporate critical thinking and implement problem-solving strategies in the development and execution of strategic plans. Demonstrate the ability to organize, direct, plan, and coordinate business operations. Build and maintain effective relationships with the Board of Commissioners, employees, tribal government officials, and volunteers. Coordinate, collaborate, and communicate with community agencies, non-profit organizations, and housing industry groups, including utility companies, on public policy initiatives and infrastructure development plans. Promote diversity, confidence, and respect within the organization and among the fourteen (14) tribes served. Demonstrate strong verbal and written communication skills, including public speaking. Exhibit effective financial management skills, including budgeting, analysis, decision-making, and reporting.

Native American Preference:

All Mission Indian Housing Authority (AMIHA) is an equal opportunity employer applying Native American Preference as defined in Section 7(b) of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Act. Submit enrollment verification with resume.

The above statements cover what are generally believed to be principal and essential functions of this job. Specific circumstances may allow or require some people assigned to the job to perform a somewhat different combination of duties.

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
About Impact Justice

Impact Justice advances safety, justice, and opportunity through boundary-breaking work that honors and empowers people and is changing expectations about what we can accomplish together. We imagine, build, and scale innovations, leverage research and other knowledge to connect the desire for change with informed action, and work to shift the narrative so that decision-makers and the public understand what’s at stake and what’s possible.

About The Menopause Project

The Menopause Project is a first-of-its-kind effort to bring comprehensive, evidence-based menopause and perimenopause care into correctional systems. Over two years, Impact Justice designed the program in close partnership with the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, and launched it across California's women's prisons in January 2026. The launch included clinical training for dozens of medical providers, a broad patient awareness campaign, and the creation of a bespoke training curriculum for Peer Support Specialists. We are now seeing positive results from the pilot and thinking about where to take the program from here.

When we began this work, our research found that no program in California — or anywhere in the United States — explicitly provided comprehensive, up-to-date menopause and perimenopause care to incarcerated women. While some corrections departments provide a basic level of care, thousands of incarcerated women across the country still lack access to what they need, and this crisis has long been absent from national conversation.

We are now entering a second and more consequential phase. In California, we are refining the model and using the state as an innovation lab for additional interventions — testing what works, at depth, in a live system. Beyond California, we are in active conversations with corrections departments in a handful of states to adapt and replicate the model. And we are carrying what we've learned well beyond correctional circles, into the clinical, research, and public conversations where this population is routinely left out.

The Program Director will lead this phase.

Who You Are

You likely have a background in public health, women’s health, or general healthcare, or experience working with incarcerated populations or other marginalized groups. You have an ethos of social justice, racial justice, community, and mutuality. You have a strong commitment to ending the criminalization of Black, Indigenous, Latine, and other people of color, financially disenfranchised people, and other marginalized groups. You have an orientation and belief that criminal justice involvement should not be an impediment to employment, career, wellness, and personal growth opportunities.

This position is the lead manager for this project. This position is external-facing and you will be skilled in public speaking and facilitation with a high degree of comfort in translating complex information to meet the needs of a myriad of audiences, including impacted populations, policymakers, health professionals, criminal justice system staff, funders, and community members.

You are a go-getter and a forward thinker!! You want to join a fast-paced Innovations team that provides the flexibility for ingenuity in the implementation of a program model. You have a background in program design, implementation, and evaluation. You are an innovative thinker who wants to be part of building and expanding programming. You can balance competing priorities, and you are simultaneously committed to the details while being able to envision, develop and implement program work that is currently in its development stages. You enjoy working both collaboratively and independently. You have a track record of effective, cross-functional collaboration across disciplines. You have highly developed interpersonal skills with good relationship-building techniques. You are a leader. You are adept at time management and highly organized with a proven ability to ensure you and a team can meet deadlines, plan, organize, and execute.

That said, we know great candidates may not think they fit what we’ve described above or may have important skills we haven’t considered. If that is you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself! We would like to hear from you even if you have most (but not all) of the skills listed. We welcome all applicants, including formerly incarcerated individuals, those with family members who have been incarcerated, and persons with direct criminal or juvenile legal system experience.

What You Will Do

The anticipated start date for this position is December 1, 2026. You will report to the Vice President of Innovation Programs. At the start of this position, you will manage one senior staff member. You’ll be the owner of The Menopause Project, and your core responsibilities will be:

Project Expansion – Strategize, manage, build out, and implement the Menopause Project expansion efforts.
Project Management – Manage various project deliverables, guide best practices and encourage iterative program refinement, manage program budget, effectively navigate challenges in program implementation, assess needs, identify helpful collaborators, and support and make high-stakes decisions.
Relationship Building – Maintain and expand partnerships with the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR), other Departments of Corrections, policymakers, non-profit and for-profit partners, and healthcare providers.
External Engagement – Participate in organizational and project-based fundraising efforts. Engage in public speaking opportunities, including media interviews, podcasts, and other events as they arise. Seek out creative fundraising strategies, e.g. public and private healthcare providers.
Advisory Board Management – Develop and implement the strategy for the program’s Advisory Board, engaging members for feedback and guidance on various aspects of the project. The position will also manage Advisory Board operations, including scheduling biannual meetings, maintaining regular email communications, and ensuring members are kept informed of program progress and impact..
Fundraising- Actively engage in fundraising efforts, including cultivating and maintaining relationships with funders, identifying new funding opportunities, and supporting proposal development and reporting.
Team Leadership – Build out a dynamic, growing team as needed, and oversee the current Senior Program Manager of the Menopause Project. Plan and implement enrichment, engagement, and camaraderie-building opportunities with the team in an effort to create an environment where each team member can thrive.
Impact Justice Leadership – Join the Impact Justice Leadership team and collaboratively work with senior and executive staff across Impact Justice and all community partners.
Supervision- At the start of this role, you will manage one senior staff member. It is anticipated that this project may add additional staffing support as budget allows and as needed. You will also work closely with the consultant who helped launch the project. The consultant will support the transition of this role and will roll off of this project in early 2027.
Travel- this position is expected to travel. Travel will include new and current project sites, as well as travel to the main Impact Justice office location, if not located in Northern California. Travel is estimated at 10%.

Education / Experience Level

Successful candidates typically have at least four years of professional training/education or closely related experience, and at least ten years of relevant experience, including at least five years of program leadership experience and at least five years of people management experience.

Required Qualifications

An adaptive problem solver with a willingness to learn and grow.
A flexible self-starter who thrives in changing, dynamic environments.
Able to juggle and implement multiple project elements.
Experience in program evaluation and program expansion.
Comfortable interacting with a wide variety of people, including individuals impacted by the criminal legal system, criminal legal system staff, officials, and individuals from diverse backgrounds and life experiences.
Experienced project manager with previous experience collecting programmatic data.
Able to build and maintain key external relationships.
An experienced and effective public speaker.
Grant/fundraising and budget management experience.
Tech-savvy: comfortable with Google Suite, Microsoft Office, Canva, etc.
A critical thinker with a high level of analytical/interpretive thinking and a positive, solutions-oriented approach to challenges.
Methodical, efficient, and able to synthesize and organize disparate information clearly.
Can hold their own with executives, funders, and public officials — professional, unintimidated, and credible as a peer in high-stakes settings.

Preferred Qualification (but Not Required)

Experienced professional within public health, women’s health, healthcare, or work with incarcerated populations with an emphasis on health.
An understanding of menopause, perimenopause care, or other related public health topics.

Applying

The position will be paid $130k- 140k. Salary offers are based on the candidate's experience and qualifications and our practice of maintaining salary equity within the organization. The benefits that come with working at Impact Justice include medical, dental, and FSA plans, significant vacation and wellness leave, and immediate vesting in our 401K with a generous match.

This is a full-time, salaried position. The candidate should be located in our Oakland, Los Angeles, or DC office and will work under a hybrid schedule. Periodic deviations to the regular hybrid schedule may be required due to program needs.

We are not considering remote staff for this position.

If This All Sounds Like a Good Fit For You, Please Include Your Resume And a Response To The Following Questions

What is your experience working in healthcare/public health and/or with incarcerated/systems-impacted people?
What is your experience building and/or sustaining a complex program or project?
Why do you believe addressing women’s health, particularly menopause and perimenopause care, in the justice system is important?
What makes you the best fit for this particular role at Impact Justice?

We plan on making decisions on a rolling basis, so the earlier you apply, the better.

Hiring Process

Elements of the Impact Justice hiring process may include phone screen interviews, candidate exercises (written or presentations), Zoom interviews, in-person interviews, and reference checks. Candidates are welcome to ask for alternative arrangements in the process if needed (for example, conducting an interview via phone rather than Zoom), Impact Justice will do our best to accommodate reasonable requests. Please communicate any alternative arrangements requested to the hiring manager.

Equal Opportunity Employment

Impact Justice provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race/ethnicity, color, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, national origin, age, criminal history, or disability.

Compensation Range: $130K - $140K

Description

About The Port Authority:

Founded in 1921, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey builds, operates, and maintains many of the most important transportation and trade infrastructure assets in the country. The agency's network of aviation, ground, rail, and seaport facilities is among the busiest in the country, supports more than 550,000 regional jobs, and generates more than twenty three billion in annual wages and eighty billion in annual economic activity. The Port Authority also owns and manages the 16-acre World Trade Center site, where the 1,776-foot-tall One World Trade Center is now the tallest skyscraper in the Western Hemisphere.

About The Port Department

The Port Department is one of the five-line department businesses of the PANYNJ. It is responsible for managing the largest port complex on the East Coast and the second largest in the nation. It operates a highly competitive and dynamic business in a very complex political environment. The Port is an economic engine that provides over 580,000 jobs in the region and nearly $240 billion in annual economic activity.

For the past 20 years, the Port has been preparing itself for the growing demand for increased trade resulting in more cargo and for the rapid migration to ever larger vessels. Together with our Port tenants, nearly $15 billion in new infrastructure, equipment and systems has been invested to ensure that Port of New York and New Jersey remains the premier East Coast gateway with even more investment in capacity planned and underway.

As a landlord Port, the Port Authority leases property to tenants that operate Port facilities. Since we do not directly handle cargo, we must influence the efficiency and productivity of the port in more strategic ways. Today, the challenges in this area continue to grow. Improving Port productivity requires a more collaborative approach. The Port Department has taken a strong leadership role in driving the changes necessary to keep the Port of New York and New Jersey highly competitive while ensuring growth in a safe, secure, sustainable and resilient way.

The Port Authority is a unique government body serving both the States of New York and New Jersey, mandated to be financially self-sufficient. As such, increasing revenues while remaining competitive is a major challenge for the Port Department moving forward.

Functional Oversight

Reporting to the Director of the Port Department, the Deputy Port Director
is a member of the senior management team of the Port Department and is responsible for oversight of the Department’s facilities, business services, commercial development, planning and capital program delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Represent the Director in all matters related to managing the Port Department, as needed.
Oversee and provide direction to the Departmental leadership that manages and directs all aspects of facility operations, maintenance, regulatory compliance (safety, security, environmental), commercial development, business services, planning and capital project delivery, while providing for meaningful and measurable improvements in how we serve the global supply chain, deliver critical infrastructure improvements, and support the communities in which we operate.
Provide strategic guidance on the development and implementation of procedures to protect existing revenue, generate new revenue sources and obtain maximum productivity/capacity of the Port facilities, control expenditures and ensuring that the department generates the maximum net contribution to the Agency.
Provide oversight, leadership, and guidance to matters associated with advancing initiatives that require inter-departmental cooperation. Work with other departments to reach consensus about roles and responsibilities, with a focus on the impact that decisions have on operations, maintenance, capital investment, sustainability, and customer service activities.
Participate in the development of the department’s strategic planning and policy agenda, business plan and support initiatives that increase revenue, reduce costs, and improve process efficiency, port efficiency, capacity, and customer service.
Provide strategic direction to all aspects of the Department’s asset management programs, including capital and operating project delivery, maintenance management and tenant support services.
Continuously review the department’s organizational structure and functions to ensure effective, efficient staff alignments that satisfy the department’s mission and vision, while supporting a work climate that embraces diversity and inclusion. Work with department leaders, to ensure staff capability, availability, competence, and motivation.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business administration, Transportation, International Trade, Logistics, Engineering or a related field from an accredited college or university. A graduate degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Transportation, Engineering, or a related field is preferred.
Minimum of 20 years of progressively responsible experience at an executive level capacity, preferably working for an organization comparable to the size and complexity of the operation in the Port of New York and New Jersey, with at least 10 years in the port and maritime transportation arena.
Must possess a valid Driver’s License and be able to obtain a Transportation Worker’s Identification Credential (TWIC) within 60 days of assuming the position.

The Ideal Candidate Will Present The Following Profile

At least 15 years of progressively responsible operations, planning, project management, customer service, performance management, property maintenance, and infrastructure management experience in a complex transportation environment.
At least 5 years of progressive responsibilities managing and directing the delivery of a broad program portfolio, measuring and improving implementation, recommending and advocating policy changes, evaluating and implementing alternate project delivery systems, and establishing and meeting Agency and Department level performance measures.
Extensive knowledge of the global supply chain and the port and maritime transportation system.
Demonstrated senior level experience in managing, leading, mentoring and developing a large diverse staff, with a proven record of effective team building and providing for successful outcomes.
Demonstrated experience in complex negotiations and conflict resolution supported by strong transactional, analytical and decision-making skills.
Superior interpersonal skills interacting with internal staff at all levels, and a broad range of external stakeholders such as government agencies, elected officials, community organizations, tenants, trade associations, contractors, consultants, and regional transportation organizations.
Demonstrated experience interacting and navigating a complex organization.
Demonstrated ability to manage conflict, build consensus, and facilitate problem solving and collaboration among various stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability developing strategies to achieve broad business goals and to understand the impact on various stakeholders/constituents within and outside of the PA.
Superior written and oral communication skills with demonstrated experience in preparing and delivering presentation materials to a broad executive and senior staff, and both internal and external stakeholders.

Compensation, Benefits & On-Site Collaboration Requirements

In accordance with Port Authority policy, this position permits employees to work remotely a maximum of one day per week. In person collaboration is essential to how the Port Authority conducts business, and regular in-office days or team collaboration days may be required on business needs.

About the Role

The Tunnels, Bridges and Terminals (TB&T) Department is seeking an experienced transportation executive to join their leadership team in the role of Deputy Director, Priority Capital Construction Programs. Reporting to the Director of TB&T, the Deputy Director provides direct oversight of a substantial capital budget and overall direction to the executive team managing the portfolio of TB&T Priority Capital Construction Programs.

This is an exciting time to join a team that is advancing several mega-projects that are vital to the regional economy, including the rehabilitation of the elevated roadway leading to the Lincoln Tunnel (the Helix), the rehabilitation of the Outerbridge Crossing, the George Washington Bridge Restore the George Program, and the $11 Billion program to replace the Port Authority Bus Terminal.

The 900 employees in the TB&T Department serve over 700,000 monthly vehicular trips across its six bridges and tunnels, which include the George Washington Bridge, Holland Tunnel, Lincoln Tunnel, Bayonne Bridge, Goethals Bridge, Outerbridge Crossing and over 200,000 passengers at Port Authority Bus Terminal and the George Washington Bridge Bus Station each day.

Responsibilities

Responsible for advancing TB&T’s Priority Capital Construction Programs and coordinating with internal and external stakeholders to advance these critical projects. The portfolio of Priority Capital Construction Programs includes:
Restore the George: This program includes a total of eleven projects valued at $2.17B. Seven of the projects are at or near completion and four remain in various stages of design/construction. The program total is valued at $2.17B in the capital plan.

The scope of work includes roadway and deck repairs required to extend the life of the bridge until it is anticipated to be replaced early in the next capital plan. jobs.description:
Company Description
The Door – A Center of Alternatives is a comprehensive youth development organization serving New York City teens and young adults ages 12–24. Under one roof, The Door offers reproductive health care and education, mental health counseling and crisis support, legal assistance, GED and ESOL classes, tutoring, and college preparation services. Young people also access career development, job training and placement, supportive housing, arts, sports, recreational activities, and nutritious meals. The organization is committed to providing inclusive, high-quality services that help participants build stability, achieve educational and career goals, and develop lifelong skills. Staff members collaborate across programs to create a welcoming, holistic environment where all young people can thrive.

Role Description
The Director of Institutional Giving is a full-time, on-site role based in Brooklyn, NY, responsible for leading and expanding The Door’s portfolio of foundation, corporate, and government funding. This position develops and implements the institutional fundraising strategy, including prospecting, cultivating relationships, and stewarding new and existing funders. Day-to-day, the Director oversees the preparation of high-quality proposals, grant reports, and supporting materials, ensuring timely submission and compliance with funder requirements. The role includes collaborating closely with program, finance, and senior leadership teams to gather data, align funding opportunities with organizational priorities, and demonstrate impact. The Director also manages tracking systems for deadlines and outcomes, monitors revenue targets, and may supervise staff or consultants engaged in institutional fundraising.

Responsibilities:

Team Leadership & Institutional Giving Operations
Manage the day-to-day operations of the Institutional Giving team, including coaching and developing three Grant Managers through regular supervision and project management
Oversee team workflow and the institutional fundraising calendar, ensuring proposals, reports, stewardship activities, and other deliverables are completed accurately and on schedule
Draft, review, and edit grant proposals, reports, letters of inquiry, budgets, and donor communications to ensure consistently high-quality submissions
Ensure the team’s timely delivery of high-quality proposals, reports, and stewardship activities

Portfolio & Relationship Managemen t

Manage and grow a portfolio of approximately 30–40 private and public institutional funders, serving as the primary relationship manager and securing renewed and new investments in support of The Door's mission and strategic priorities

jobs.description:
Are you ready to make an impact at DTCC?

Do you want to work on innovative projects, collaborate with a dynamic and supportive team, and receive investment in your professional development? At DTCC, we are at the forefront of innovation in the financial markets. We are committed to helping our employees grow and succeed. We believe that you have the skills and drive to make a real impact. We foster a thriving internal community and are committed to creating a workplace that looks like the world that we serve.

The General Counsel's Office is a valued, trusted and responsive partner within DTCC. The team promotes and protects the best interests of the DTCC family of companies by creating and facilitating solutions and providing guidance on legal and regulatory matters.

Pay And Benefits

Competitive compensation, including base pay and annual incentive
Comprehensive health and life insurance and well-being benefits, based on location
Pension / Retirement benefits
Paid Time Off and Personal/Family Care, and other leaves of absence when needed to support your physical, financial, and emotional well-being.
DTCC offers a flexible/hybrid model of 3 days onsite and 2 days remote (onsite Tuesdays, Wednesdays and a third day unique to each team or employee).

The Impact You Will Have In This Role

The Executive Director for Business Compliance is responsible for supporting the business's identification, development and monitoring of key controls leveraged by DTCC to maintain compliance with its regulatory requirements, primarily Covered Clearing Agency Standards ("CCAS"). The function maintains a centralized inventory of regulatory requirements for DTCC Businesses, facilitates mapping of those requirements to controls and conducts monitoring and testing to validate the controls are fit for purpose and adhered to. In addition, the function monitors Policy and Procedures that demonstrate compliance with the Business's regulatory requirements and works with management to address gaps and inconsistencies. The function is also the primary Compliance interface for exams and monitors for trends, guidance and new regulations which impact the Business and require enhancements to the existing compliance control framework. Additionally, the group prepares reports on the status of the program to Board, Committees and senior management.

Your Primary Responsibilities

Develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of applicable laws and regulations applicable to the covered Business areas, as well as requirements and resulting controls that enable compliance.
Evaluate Business related compliance requirements and readiness for any new initiative or business venture
Monitor for new or changing regulations and assess the Business’s readiness for compliance.
Develop and maintain a risk-based continuous evaluation of existing processes and related controls to challenge adequacy relative to the existing regulations and best practices
Work with applicable areas to develop action plans for development and enhancement of compliance controls and provide ongoing support and monitoring of the implementation of those controls
Support Regulatory Relations, GCO and Business areas in regulatory examinations, inspections and inquiries.
Advance DTCC’s response time to address compliance gaps or weaknesses
Monitor regulatory trends and actions to proactively anticipate future areas of regulatory focus
Working in partnership with Compliance Risk Assessment and Testing, monitor key inherently high-risk compliance requirements and the design and effectiveness of the processes, controls, and metrics within DTCC Businesses related to compliance with regulatory requirements (e.g. CCAS, Reg SCI, etc.)
Monitor DTCC Policies and Procedures to maintain compliance with key regulations and identify and address any gaps or inconsistencies and test/monitor for adherence to key controls
Communicate key Compliance program statuses, issues, and escalation of key risks via maintenance and production of Board, Committee and Management reporting of compliance program effectiveness, issues, risk tolerances, operational risk profiles and key metrics
Support and monitor ongoing staff education and development in effective risk management
Serve as key member of compliance management team globally, including compliance with all applicable global regulations and guidance
Oversee teams’ partnership with the Businesses, Legal department and other second line control. Serve as a senior liaison on cross-functional teams
Partner with DTCC management to ensure that compliance programs and measures are aligned with the overall corporate compliance strategy (including programs related to legal review and risk initiatives)
Fosters a risk management culture through implementation and demonstration of processes and procedures which identify and mitigate risk

Qualifications:- Minimum of 15 years of related experience

Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent experience

Talents Needed for Success:- Strong knowledge of clearing agencies and regulatory environments

Knowledge of banking and securities laws including Standards for Covered Clearing Agencies
Knowledge of both domestic and global markets preferred
Excellent listening and communication (oral and written) skills to effectively interface with all levels of leadership
A highly organized and disciplined individual able to effectively develop as well as manage and influence a team of experienced professionals across a global organization

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Lead WPSR into its next chapter as its new Executive Director

Washington Physicians for Social Responsibility (WPSR) works at the intersection of health, policy, and social change. We believe that health professionals have a unique responsibility—and a powerful voice—in addressing the most urgent threats facing humanity: nuclear weapons, climate change, and economic inequity. For over 45 years, WPSR has mobilized health professionals and community advocates across Washington State to advance policies that protect human health and promote a more just, peaceful, and sustainable future.

Our impact is driven by a committed member and volunteer base, a collaborative and mission-driven staff, and strong partnerships across movements. Grounded in health equity, WPSR leverages the trusted authority of health professionals to address the underlying drivers of injustice and drive bold policy change. WPSR is both an independent organization and part of a larger national and international movement of health professionals working to address existential threats to human health.

Our strength comes from the combination of expertise and action: we bring the trusted voice of health professionals into public debates while building the civic power necessary to create meaningful change.
WPSR is seeking a dynamic and strategic Executive Director to lead the organization into its next phase of growth and impact. This leader will bring a deep commitment to our mission, strong organizational and relationship-building skills, and a demonstrated ability to guide a nonprofit organization with clarity, integrity, and vision.

This is a full-time, hybrid, exempt position reporting to the Board of Directors. WPSR’s office is located in Seattle’s North Beacon Hill neighborhood.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership & Program Impact

The Executive Director provides vision and direction for WPSR’s programs, ensuring that our advocacy, education, and organizing efforts are aligned, effective, and impactful.

Partner with the Board to establish organizational strategy, priorities, and annual plans
Support program leaders in advancing goals across WPSR’s issue areas
Oversee program staffing, grants, deliverables, and public-facing communications
Ensure WPSR’s work continues to advance health, equity, and justice

Fundraising & Sustainability

The Executive Director leads efforts to build the resources needed to sustain and expand WPSR’s impact.

Develop and manage the annual budget and revenue strategy
Build relationships with individual donors, foundations, institutional funders, and partners
Partner with the Board on fundraising strategy and donor engagement
Lead grant development, fundraising campaigns, and events

Board Partnership & Governance

The Executive Director works closely with the Board to support strong governance and organizational accountability.

Collaborate with Board leadership on strategy, governance, and organizational priorities
Provide regular updates on programs, finances, and organizational performance
Support effective board engagement and committee work
Maintain compliance with bylaws and legal requirements

People & Organizational Culture

The Executive Director cultivates an inclusive, supportive, and high-performing workplace where staff and volunteers can thrive.

Lead recruitment, supervision, performance management, and professional development
Maintain effective HR systems, policies, and practices
Foster a culture grounded in collaboration, equity, and shared purpose

Operations & Organizational Management

The Executive Director ensures that WPSR operates effectively, transparently, and sustainably.

Oversee financial management in partnership with the Treasurer and Board
Maintain strong operational systems, including technology, databases, and recordkeeping
Ensure compliance with organizational policies and applicable regulations

External Relations & Visibility

As WPSR’s primary representative, the Executive Director builds relationships and elevates the organization’s voice.

Represent WPSR with coalitions, partners, policymakers, and community leaders
Serve as liaison to national Physicians for Social Responsibility and other chapters
Oversee communications and strengthen WPSR’s public visibility

Membership Engagement & Growth

The Executive Director strengthens WPSR’s community of members and supporters.

Build meaningful relationships with members and volunteers
Expand and diversify membership
Create opportunities for engagement and leadership

﻿QUALIFICATIONS

There is no single professional background that defines the ideal candidate. We are looking for someone with demonstrated leadership experience who is energized by mission-driven work and capable of bringing people together around ambitious goals.

The strongest candidates will bring many of the following qualities:

A compelling commitment to WPSR’s mission and values.
Significant experience leading a nonprofit, advocacy organization, campaign, coalition, or comparable mission-driven enterprise.
Strategic vision combined with the ability to translate ideas into action.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Significant experience with and success in fundraising, donor relationships, and organizational development.
A demonstrated ability to build authentic relationships across differences.
Experience supervising, mentoring, inspiring, and developing staff.
Comfort working in political and policy environments.
The ability to balance urgency and ambition with sound organizational management.
Intellectual curiosity, humility, resilience, creativity, and a good sense of humor.

We strongly encourage people from historically underrepresented communities and people with diverse professional and lived experiences to apply.
We believe that the movement for a healthier and more just world is stronger when leadership reflects the communities we seek to serve.

Benefits & Compensation

This is a full-time, exempt position that requires occasional evening and weekend work. It is eligible for our benefits package that includes medical and dental (100% employer paid), employee-funded Flexible Spending Account, 401k with a modest employer match most years, 10 paid holidays, paid sick leave, and 4 weeks paid vacation.

Compensation is $110K-$125K per year.

In line with our commitment to equity practices, the salary for this position has been carefully determined to reflect market standards and internal equity considerations. We value the skills and expertise that each candidate brings to the table, and we believe that our non-negotiable salary approach fosters a level playing field for all applicants. This practice aligns with our core values of transparency and fairness. All submissions are reviewed by humans – there is no AI used in our hiring process.

How to Apply

Complete applications submitted with a thoughtful cover letter will be reviewed on a rolling basis
, and the position will remain open until filled. All applications must be submitted online. No phone calls, please.
We seek to recruit and retain talented applicants from a diverse candidate pool. We especially welcome applicants who support our organization’s core values: science, sustainability, compassion, peace, justice, and equity. WPSR provides equal employment opportunities with no discrimination against any individual with respect to compensation, terms, conditions, or privileges of employment because of race, color, age, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, or disability.

Thank you for your interest! To learn more about our organization, please visit www.wpsr.org.

jobs.company: Texarkana Regional Arts and Humanities Council, Inc.
jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
For nearly five decades, the Texarkana Regional Arts & Humanities Council (TRAHC) has been bringing people and community together through the arts. Founded in 1978, TRAHC’s mission is to grow people and community through the arts, creating opportunities for people of all ages and backgrounds to experience, explore, and engage with the arts. Today, TRAHC continues to build on that legacy through an expanding range of cultural, educational, and creative programming. With two unique community facilities, a growing team, and a vision for continued impact, TRAHC offers an exciting opportunity for a visionary leader to help shape the organization’s next chapter.

The Executive Director manages a dynamic team of 10-15 individuals including coordinators and directors, as well as part-time attendants and additionally oversees operations in two community facilities: the Regional Arts Center and TRAHC’s ArtSpace. The Regional Arts Center, an artisan-restored former federal courthouse dating to 1911, is TRAHC’s formal event space, featuring office space, galleries for installations and exhibits, and party, rental, and event space. TRAHC’s ArtSpace (within walking distance of the Regional Arts Center) is a multi-use, multi-disciplinary community art space that offers professional development, workshops, and classes, with event and rental space, along with staff offices and supply rooms.
This position works closely with the Board of Directors and, with their assistance and guidance, the Executive Director is responsible for the executive, managerial, fiscal, programmatic, and operational success of the organization. The Executive Director builds on TRAHC’s 48 years of enriching community programming and provides leadership for TRAHC’s two facilities, ensuring that each effectively and thoroughly supports the organization’s mission, programs, and long-term growth in the 4 States Region.

What your essential functions will be:

The Executive Director of TRAHC will coordinate the arts council’s strategic planning and vision in the Texarkana community, while managing staff at the two facilities and promoting the organization to members and patrons of the community. Some functions of this position will include:

Meet with community members, funders, and patrons to tell and promote the story of the arts council, as well as contextualize its impact
Research, develop, and lead robust fundraising efforts (both existing and new)
Maintain, grow, and optimize internal systems such as:
Financial (e.g., oversight of budgetary process and expenditure of funds),  
Operational resources (e.g., vendors, equipment, software,); and
Databases on students, donors, and artists/instructors
Oversee the effective operation, maintenance, use, and development of both TRAHC Facilities
Coordinate and advise a team of specialized staff including: administration, marketing and media, education, events and rentals, and visual arts/studio programs 
Collaborate with key local and regional representatives on current projects
Coordinate, plan, network and fundraise for future success
Develop and implement strategies that maximize the use and impact of both the Regional Arts Center and TRAHC’s ArtSpace
Identify opportunities and plan for growth across TRAHC’s two spaces and across departments
Ensure operational attunement with organizational mission, purpose, and values

Who will be successful in this role:

The Executive Director of TRAHC is a dynamic forward-looking position that draws on an appreciation of community education, civic engagement and public outreach, the arts, and an economical understanding of nonprofit finances in the context of an ever-changing funding environment. The following characteristics illustrate who would be successful in this role:
a background in nonprofit management, business administration, public policy, or a related field
an appreciation for the arts (multidisciplinary)
an understanding of fundraising, writing grants, and developing revenue sources
the ability to take and delegate responsibilities across staff
excellent project management and organizational skills
public speaking, networking, and public relations skills
passion for the community served through the organization’s programs and mission

Why this position is significant:

jobs.description:
The YMCA of Florida's First Coast seeks an Executive Director to empower people, strengthen communities, and create opportunity.

Job Description

About the Brooks Family YMCA

A growing wellness-focused YMCA distinguished by its partnership with Brooks Rehabilitation and innovative Urban Court community engagement model.

The Brooks Family YMCA serves one of Jacksonville's fastest-growing communities and has become a destination where individuals and families come together to pursue healthier lives, build meaningful relationships, and experience a true sense of belonging.

What makes Brooks especially unique is its longstanding relationship with Brooks Rehabilitation. Built on a shared commitment to health, wellness, and improving quality of life, this partnership creates opportunities for innovation while reinforcing the YMCA's role as a trusted community resource where people can thrive physically, socially, and emotionally.

The branch is also home to the recently added Urban Court, a vibrant outdoor gathering space designed to bring people together through recreation, connection, and community.

More than a place for sports, the Urban Court serves as a neighborhood hub where youth, adults, and families build relationships, stay active, and create lasting memories. It reflects the YMCA's commitment to breaking down barriers, fostering belonging, and creating accessible opportunities for people of all ages to connect.

As the surrounding community continues to grow, so does the opportunity for the YMCA to deepen its impact. The Executive Director will have the opportunity to develop a high-performing team, cultivate emerging leaders, strengthen strategic partnerships, and help shape the future of one of the association's most innovative and fast-growing branches. For leaders energized by growth, collaboration, and community building, Brooks offers an exceptional opportunity to lead with purpose and vision.

Lead with Purpose. Build Community. Change Lives.

We are seeking a mission-driven, strategic, and relationship-focused leader who is a passionate and forward-thinking executive with a proven track record of advancing organizational impact. The ideal candidate will demonstrate success in developing and engaging a strong branch board, growing philanthropic support through annual giving, strengthening community relationships, increasing membership and program participation, and leading initiatives that expand the YMCA’s mission and impact within the community.

Why the YMCA?

Working For The YMCA Means Joining a Cause-driven Organization Dedicated To Strengthening Communities Through Youth Development, Healthy Living, And Social Responsibility. As a Branch Executive Director, You Will

Make a meaningful impact in the lives of children, families, and seniors.

Lead a talented and dedicated team of staff and volunteers.

Build relationships that create lasting community change.

Develop innovative programs that meet critical community needs.

Grow professionally through leadership development opportunities and YMCA networks.

A history of success in:
Financial and budget management
Staff supervision and team development
Strategic planning and goal achievement
Community partnership development
Membership and program management
Must pass Level 2 Background Screening. Level 2 is a fingerprint check of state and federal criminal history information conducted through the Florida Department of law Enforcement (FDLE) and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). https://info.flclearinghouse.com

Essential Functions

Develop, manage, and monitor the branch operating and capital budgets to achieve financial sustainability and revenue growth.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Events & Transportation
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) seeks applications and nominations for an accomplished, strategic and service-oriented leader to serve as Executive Director, Events & Transportation (E&T)
. This highly visible role shapes how people access, move through and experience the UCLA campus - from daily mobility and parking to major events, ticketing and community-facing operations.

The Executive Director leads a broad portfolio at the intersection of transportation, events, customer experience, sustainability and campus operations. The portfolio includes transportation demand management; parking and traffic systems; campus transit; bicycle, micromobility and pedestrian safety; shared mobility; public transit partnerships; fleet acquisition and maintenance; commuter programs; event and film-shoot access to campus spaces; and the Central Ticket Office (CTO), which supports ticketing for thousands of events annually.

The scope and complexity of E&T offer an exceptional platform for a leader who can connect long-range strategy with operational excellence. The Executive Director oversees a transportation and events enterprise with more than $78 million in revenues, a combined operating budget exceeding $48.5 million, annual debt service/non-operating expense of $5.5 million, and a staff of nearly 300 FTE/headcount of 485. The organization also manages substantial physical and financial assets and provides important financial support to campus programs.

Operationally, the portfolio includes a 22,000+ space parking system across more than 50 facilities; a fleet of approximately 950 University vehicles (including 50% zero-emission vehicles); nearly half a million annual transit boardings with directly operated service; agreements with seven local transit agencies, including more than 400 public transit buses visiting campus each weekday; approximately 84,000 daily vehicle trips;; more than 3,000 bicycle parking spaces; and 800 shared micromobility modes. E&T also supports 850 annual campus events and extra-curricular activities including high-profile events such as UCLA Commencement with up to 65,000 daily attendees and provides strategic oversight of CTO ticketing services for 8,000+ campus events annually.

The Executive Director establishes the long-term vision and strategy for a sustainable, accessible, safer, and well-connected UCLA campus, balancing service excellence, sound business practices, regulatory requirements, and the needs of the University and surrounding communities. The leader oversees Commuter & Parking Services, Events, Fleet & Transit, Mobility Planning & Traffic Systems, and the Central Ticket Office, driving operational excellence, innovation, and integrated transportation and event strategies. The role provides strategic leadership for major transportation and campus-planning initiatives, including the Metro D Line Subway Extension and the Sepulveda Transit Corridor subway project, while representing UCLA with government agencies, transit partners, community organizations, and industry stakeholders to advocate for campus interests and expanded sustainable mobility. The Executive Director also leads long-range financial and operational planning across multiple multi-million-dollar enterprises, including pricing, revenue management, asset stewardship, and performance measurement; oversees coordination of major campus events; and advances technology, process improvements, and customer-focused services across transportation, parking, traffic, fleet, events, and ticketing operations.

The ideal candidate will be an accomplished leader who combines enterprise-scale operational leadership, sophisticated stakeholder management, and strong business judgment, with the ability to operate effectively in a highly visible and politically sensitive environment and navigate the complexities of an urban transportation ecosystem with competing resource demands. The successful candidate will have demonstrated experience leading large, complex organizations and diverse workforces, along with strong budgetary and strategic planning capabilities, exceptional relationship-building skills, and highly developed negotiation, collaboration, and communication abilities. They will bring strong business and political acumen, including the ability to advocate effectively at federal, state, and regional levels; analyze qualitative and quantitative information, trends, and policies; and translate insights into organizational strategies, focused plans, and sound decisions. Knowledge of applicable state, federal, and local industry trends, and sustainable transportation fundamentals is essential, as is human resources leadership experience in a primarily unionized environment. Familiarity with University policies, programs, and management practices is preferred.

The Executive Director is entrusted with significant University assets and is expected to exercise a high degree of prudence and integrity. E&T is responsible for construction and maintenance associated with more than 7.6 million square feet of facilities with an approximate asset value of $767.97 million, as well as debt-capacity analysis related to more than $45.1 million in long-term financing.

To apply for the position, please submit a resume as well as a cover letter that expands upon your relevant experience, prior roles held and specific accomplishments within those roles.

Salary & Compensation

UCLA provides a full pay range. Actual salary offers consider factors, including budget, prior experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business considerations. Salary offers at the top of the range are not common. Visit UC Benefit package to discover benefits that start on day one, and UC Total Compensation Estimator to calculate the total compensation value with benefits.

Qualifications

1. Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain strong and enduring relationships with a wide variety of constituencies, including faculty, staff, students, University administrators, community leaders, government officials, the general public, and the media. (Required)
2. Skill in negotiating and in exchanging ideas, information and opinions with a variety of constituencies to formulate policies and programs, and arrive jointly at decisions, conclusions or solutions. (Required)
3. Highly developed and effective verbal communication skills for making persuasive oral presentations to senior management, as well as internal and external constituencies, and to conduct participatory meetings, gain acceptance of decision, and to advise and collaborate with others. Demonstrated written communication skill to prepare concise, logical, accurate, and grammatically correct reports, presentations, project proposals, correspondence, etc. to address sensitive, complex and broad ranging issues in a university and business setting. (Required)
4. Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively and respectfully with a variety of constituencies, with multiple interests, to define and achieve organizational objectives. (Required)
5. Demonstrated ability to perform with a high degree of composure, judgment and political acumen to effectively address varied issues of a politically sensitive, highly visible or closely scrutinized nature. (Required)
6. Demonstrated business and political acumen, and the ability to advocate effectively at federal, state and regional levels. (Required)
7. Knowledge of applicable state, federal and local ordinances, codes, laws, rules and regulations, and legislative issues. (Required)
8. Demonstrated ability to manage a large, complex organization with a highly diverse staff and student body, including budgetary and strategic planning skills. (Required)
9. Demonstrated knowledge of the principles of human resources, and the ability to apply these principles in a primarily unionized environment and in accordance with collective bargaining agreements. (Required)
10. Demonstrated ability to clearly and logically analyze qualitative and quantitative information, trends and policies; ability to develop broad organizational assessments and initiatives, as well as more selected and focused plans, solutions and advice. (Required)
11. Knowledge and understanding of University policies, programs and management principles, practices and trends. Ability to apply policy to ensure fair and consistent outcomes. Including knowledge and understanding of University policies and strategies related to inclusive excellence. Ability to collaborate with senior leaders to integrate EDI policies and best practices into workplace practices and programs. (Preferred)
12. Knowledge of sustainable transportation fundamentals. (Required)

Education, Licenses, Certifications & Personal Affiliations

Must possess, upon hire, and maintain a valid CA noncommercial Class C License in accordance with the California (CA) Department of Motor Vehicles. (Required)

Special Conditions for Employment

jobs.title: Executive Director, Pollution Control Services
jobs.description:
Position Description

Harris County Pollution Control Services Department (HCPCS)
Mission:

The mission of Harris County Pollution Control Services Department (PCS) is to protect the citizens of Harris County from environmental impacts through firm, consistent enforcement of state and federal regulations. The ultimate goal of PCS is clean air, water, and proper management of waste. The activities PCS are directed toward ensuring clean air and water for the citizens of Harris County, consistent with the protection of public health, enjoyment of property and the protection of plant, animal, and marine life.

Position Overview:

Under the direction of the County Administrator, the Executive Director of Pollution Control (ED) is responsible for providing leadership, management, and oversight over all Harris County Pollution Control Services (HCPCS) operations, including developing, implementing, and maintaining the Department's mission, vision, and strategic plan. In addition, the Executive Director is responsible for reviewing and commenting on requests for permits, driving countywide sustainability and climate action strategies, developing and implementing departmental policies, including community monitoring. The ED will ensure compliance and enforcement of environmental rules, regulations, and laws as outlined in County regulations, State and Federal statutes, and/or adopted by State and Federal regulatory agencies.

The Executive Director will lead in educating the public on various sources of environmental risk and preventive measures to protect their communities, and will serve as an advocate for sound environmental and pollution control policies at the local, state, and federal levels, thereby advancing the quality of life for all residents of Harris County.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Executive Leadership: Provides broad oversight of Pollution Control Services (PCS) operations and staff by directing the work of divisions through division managers, section supervisors, and support staff; executes the department's mission, vision, strategic plan, goals, and objectives; and oversees recruitment, onboarding, training, and employee development to ensure departmental operations align with organizational priorities and desired outcomes. Reports to the Commissioner’s Court regularly and leads initiatives and achieves goals set by the Harris County Strategic Plan.
Budget and Resource Management: Guides departmental requests, budget preparation, and provides primary fiscal oversight of departmental general funds and grants; evaluates resource needs to support departmental programs, operations, staffing, contracts, and strategic priorities.
Executive Leadership: Provides broad oversight of Pollution Control Services (PCS) operations and staff by directing the work of divisions through division managers, section supervisors, and support staff; executes the department's mission, vision, strategic plan, goals, and objectives; and oversees recruitment, onboarding, training, and employee development to ensure departmental operations align with organizational priorities and desired outcomes.
Budget and Resource Management: Guides departmental requests, budget preparation, and provides primary fiscal oversight of departmental general funds and grants; evaluates resource needs to support departmental programs, operations, staffing, contracts, and strategic priorities.
Programmatic and Regulatory Oversight: Establishes measurable departmental goals and objectives and oversees core environmental programs and operations, including field monitoring, inspections, sampling, laboratory testing, data collection, community monitoring, and related regulatory activities. Oversees the development and implementation of community monitoring strategies and evaluates departmental operations to achieve environmental and public health outcomes. In addition, provides technical and policy support to County departments in developing internal pollution-mitigation and sustainability strategies that comply with applicable local, state, and federal requirements.
Compliance, Enforcement, and Permitting: Ensures federal, state, and local environmental laws, rules, regulations, and statutes are appropriately interpreted and applied through departmental monitoring, compliance, and enforcement activities. Oversees regulatory actions, including the issuance of Violation Notices, recommendations for civil and criminal cases, fines, penalties, and compliance and enforcement actions. Reviews and comments on environmental permits and related regulatory matters to prevent or minimize adverse impacts on the environment and public health.
Environmental Policy and Legislative Affairs: Develops, directs, and evaluates departmental environmental policies, procedures, and strategic initiatives to ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations; leads the development and advancement of pollution control, environmental protection, and climate-related policy priorities; monitors, analyzes, and interprets legislative and regulatory developments at the local, state, and federal levels; and provides experts recommendations, policy guidance, and formal responses to Commissioners Court and other governing bodies as required. Identifies opportunities for changes to environmental policies, rules, regulations, and law and advocates for appropriate changes through established channels.
Intergovernmental and Community Partnerships: Develops and maintains effective working relationships with local, state, and federal agencies and participates in multi-jurisdictional compliance and enforcement activities; establishes cooperation agreements involving data and resource sharing with Harris County departments, other governmental entities, and nongovernmental organizations. Represents PCS in intergovernmental matters and advances coordinated approaches to environmental protection and pollution control.
Environmental Response and Legal Support: Provides departmental leadership during environmental emergencies and may serve in Incident or Unified Command structures; oversees environmental response activities, including air, soil, and surface water monitoring; coordinates departmental response efforts with the County's Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Management and other response partners; and represents the department in legal proceedings and provides testimony as required.
Public and Media Relations: Represents PCS before professionals, community stakeholders, governmental entities, and the general public; conducts presentations and educational activities regarding environmental and public health issues; develops and implements strategies to increase public awareness of PCS activities and environmental risks; educates the public regarding environmental risks and preventive measures; responds to media inquiries and interview requests; and serves as an advocate for sound environmental and pollution control policies at the local, state, and federal levels.

Other Duties:

This Job Description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this position. Management may, at its discretion, assign, or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Employees are responsible for executing the duties and responsibilities listed above, as well as any other duties as assigned. Some positions may require employees to work before, during, or after an emergency or disaster, at the department's discretion.

Harris County is an Equal Opportunity Employer

If you need special services or accommodations, please call (713) 274-5445 or email ADACoordinator@bmd.hctx.net .

This position is subject to a criminal history check. Only relevant convictions will be considered and, even when considered, may not automatically disqualify the candidate.

Requirements

Cover Letter
Resume

Education and Experience:

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Toxicology, Environmental Science, Environmental Policy, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, or a related field.
Five (5) years of experience supervising professional staff in relevant environmental enforcement fields, including experience with environmental policy, pollution control and response, environmental toxicology, and/or emergency response.

Additional experience may be substituted for education on a year-for-year basis.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Knowledge and understanding of principles, practices, and program areas related to environmental toxicology, technical air, water, and soil pollution control functions and activities.
Broad knowledge and understanding of current developments, literature, and sources of information regarding air, water, and soil quality management.
Working knowledge of environmental policy, pollution control and response, environmental toxicology and/or emergency response.
Working knowledge of current environmental regulatory issues and a strong understanding of relevant rules, regulations, and laws/statutes.
Working knowledge of sustainability strategies, energy and technology solutions that address climate.
Must possess demonstrated leadership skills.
Must have staff development and management experience including but not limited to planning, organizing, coordinating, directing, budgeting, and fiscal management.
Skilled in exercising sound independent judgment within policy guidelines.
Ability to effectively communicate and work with leadership teams and the public.
Proficient use of computer software for email communication, budget management, and database retrieval.

Work Environment, Physical and Mental Demands:

The work is performed in an office environment, where the use of standard office equipment such as computers, phones, scanners, and filing cabinets is routine to perform the essential functions of the position.
This position requires sedentary work, including sitting for extended periods, with the ability to use and perform repetitive motion and manual dexterity. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to perform the essential functions of this job successfully.
The work requires high levels of concentration and attention to detail, high levels of creativity and innovation, high levels of work-related stress, and high levels of memory and information retention to perform the essential functions of the position.
