new_jobs.title: Development Director
new_jobs.description:
Innocence & Justice Louisiana (IJLA) is seeking a Development Director. The Development Director will play an important role in ensuring the financial stability and future growth of IJLA. The Development Director is responsible for leading and planning comprehensive fundraising and stewardship initiatives and activities to fully support the mission and the work of IJLA.

The Development Director will report directly to the Deputy Director and will work closely with the leadership and management teams at IJLA. The Development Director will supervise the Development Coordinator. This is a full-time, in-person position at IJLA.

About IJLA

Innocence & Justice Louisiana frees innocent people sentenced to prison and those serving unjust sentences. We recognize the root causes of wrongful convictions and unjust sentences as systemic racism and inequity. We work to expose and address these root causes by securing the release of the wrongfully convicted and unjustly punished; sharing our clients’ stories in court, the legislature, the community, and the media; and supporting our clients to enable them to live well and fully in the world after their release.

Responsibilities & Duties:

Development
Oversee and manage development and fundraising efforts for IJLA.
Create a comprehensive and diversified development plan on an annual basis in alignment with strategic and budgetary goals/priorities/needs.
Evaluate success against the development plan with data analysis and benchmarking.
Be primary point of contact and staff manager for external fundraising / event committees, supporting their work with materials, guidance, and oversight.

Donor Engagement & Stewardship
Own a portfolio of donor relationships and manage local and national donor engagement through e-mail, phone, and/or in-person meetings.
Develop and execute a stewardship strategy on an annual basis.
Set strategy for new donor prospect research and donor reengagement in partnership with other team members.
Be responsible for CRM leadership and ensure the implementation of best practices to ensure CRM data quality, and accurate tracking of donor engagement.
Evaluate the donor experience and communicate and incorporate feedback to team members, as appropriate.

Grants
Manage grant strategy, including identifying new grant opportunities and handling relationships with grant and foundation managers.
Prepare grant applications, and/or oversee the grant writing process by others, tracking major milestones and responsible parties to ensure timely submission of letters of intent, applications, and submission requirements.
Ensure the tracking of grant awards and rejections and when available, analyze and incorporate feedback and recommendations into future proposals and strategy.
Work with the leadership and operations to transition grants to appropriate parties with clear expectations, future requirements and reporting milestones.

Events
Oversee the creation and management of an annual event calendar.
Establish the budget, fundraising goals, and content and themes for all events.
Spearhead the selection of venues and vendors, including contracting in collaboration with operations and leadership.
Develop standardized templates for event hosting, with workplans that include major milestones and responsible parties, due dates, and event run of shows, and related event policies and procedures.
Conduct post-event analysis and compile lessons learned and key takeaways.
In collaboration with Communications, create event promotions and community outreach strategy and materials.
Manage event host committees, sponsorships and conduct sponsor outreach.
Manage event donor and sponsor stewardship post events.

Communications
With the Communications Manager, identify compelling stories to highlight IJLA’s work, including the impact on clients, to support fundraising efforts and grant applications.

Qualifications:
Minimum of 5-7 years of experience in fundraising, preferably for a non-profit organization. A plus – experience in criminal legal aid/reform organizations or similar social justice work.
Hands-on experience in donor relations, major gift solicitation, campaign management, and event planning, including large events.
Demonstrated success in grant-writing – securing, and managing government, corporate, and foundation grants.
Strong relationship-building, leadership and management experience.
Ability to design long-term fundraising campaigns and revenue strategies, analyze fundraising trends, and manage multi-project pipelines.
Excellent written, verbal, and public speaking abilities to pitch donors and inspire teams. Ability to communicate clearly and effectively to diverse internal and external audiences.
Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail; ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
Proficiency with customer relationship management (CRM), donor management software, and MS Office Suite.
Experience using data, metrics, and reporting to inform decisions and drive performance.
Past supervisory/coaching/mentorship experience.
Ability to work both independently and in a collaborative setting. A self-starter who asks questions and seeks clarification, when needed.
Ability to travel.
Willingness to work irregular hours and weekends for events or to meet deadlines when necessary.
Valid driver’s license.

Salary & Benefits:

The salary range for this position is $80,000 – $90,000. Salary will be commensurate with relevant experience. IJLA offers a very competitive benefits package, including medical/dental/vision and six weeks of paid vacation, 401k match, and cell phone reimbursement. IJLA is a family and pet friendly workplace.

Application

Applications will be considered on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Please e-mail a cover letter, resume, writing sample, and three references to openings@justicelouisiana.org. Please include the job title in the e-mail subject line. Please do not call. Only applicants selected for interviews will be contacted.
IJLA is an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse workforce reflective of the diverse communities we serve and support. IJLA works to advance racial justice and equity. We value diverse experiences, including with regard to educational background and legal system contact, and depend on a diverse staff to carry out our mission.

The primary responsibility of the Development Director is to develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising plan that includes major contributions, corporate and foundation giving, planned giving, and special events. 

Responsibilities:

Assist in the collaborative effort of researching individuals, corporations, foundations, and government entities identified by the President & CEO and by leadership volunteers as potential sources of funding. This research will include personal interactions and the application of professional best practices.
In collaboration with Senior Leadership, develop appropriate outreach strategies to accompany established fundraising goals.
Develop and execute an annual fundraising plan in collaboration with the President & CEO, Advancement team, and Board of Directors, including strategies for individual giving, major contributions, corporate and private partnerships, grants, and special events.
Cultivate and steward relationships with current and prospective donors, including individuals, corporations, foundations, lending institutions, and government entities to maximize philanthropic support for CUL.
Identify and research new funding opportunities, grant prospects, and partnership opportunities aligned with the organization’s mission and initiatives.
Plan and execute fundraising events and campaigns, including donor cultivation events, online campaigns, and peer to peer fundraising initiatives in both the public and private sectors.
Oversee the grant management process, forecasting, mapping, grant submission and reporting.
Collaborate with program leaders and grant writer to develop compelling grant proposals, reports, and fundraising materials that effectively communicate the impact and outcomes of CUL’s programs and initiatives.
Oversee lead writer and facilitator for all grant writing.
Create and ensure timely tracking of fundraising activities, donor communications, and grant reporting using donor management software and other tools.
Manage and analyze fundraising reports, contact and giving history as it pertains to ongoing strategic projections.
Act on behalf of CUL Senior Leadership and serve as a spokesperson for grant management process and updates.
Develop stewardship tools such as engagement activities, advocacy, and volunteerism, recognition opportunities and sponsorship packages.
Provide oversite and evaluate the effectiveness of fundraising strategies and ensure continuous improvement based on data and best practices.
Stay informed about trends and developments in philanthropy, fundraising, local and state communities, and the nonprofit sector; and integrate innovative approaches and technologies into CUL’s fundraising efforts.
Other duties as assigned.

·        Effective and professional verbal and written communication skills
·        Strong interpersonal and customer service skills
·         Impeccable integrity
·         Ability to work with individuals from all backgrounds with varying needs
·         Enthusiastic team player

·        Commitment to compliance and ethical standards
·        Experience with videoconferencing systems (e.g., Webex, Zoom, Teams, etc.)

Time Management and Organization:

·        Ensures accuracy, efficiency, and consistency across all tasks

new_jobs.title: Director of Development, College of Medicine
new_jobs.description:
Department

FSU Division of University Advancement

Florida State University is currently in the leadership phase of a comprehensive campaign. As the leadership phase of the campaign begins, the Division of University Advancement is accelerating the hiring of additional development officers’ campus-wide and is excited to build out its team. For Advancement professionals who are interested in being a part of a comprehensive campaign from the beginning for their career development, the timing is ideal to join our team.

Responsibilities

The Director of Development will strategically execute a personal solicitation program resulting in philanthropic support by maximizing the identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of prospects for gifts at the $100,000 and up level for College of Medicine. This individual will secure, on an annual basis, private support at the major and principal gift level and will be responsible for identification of potential major and principal gift prospects. The Director of Development will be expected to uphold and exemplify the operating practices of the Division of University Advancement while raising philanthropic dollars in support of the mission of Florida State University.

Works with the Dean, and the other members of the College of Medicine development, communication and alumni team to develop and execute strategic fundraising initiatives on behalf of the College and the university. Develops, coordinates, and executes an annual major gift plan, implementing fund-raising activities designed to meet an established monetary goal while also hitting a set suite of metrics. Establishes new relationships resulting in philanthropic investment, maintains existing relationships, which may generate new philanthropic investments, and provides prospect/donor-related assessments and feedback for the College and the Division of University Advancement. Identifies, qualifies and sustains a donor prospect portfolio with individuals who have a giving capacity of $500,000 or more. Travels frequently, and secures gifts and pledges from alumni, parents, faculty, staff, and friends of FSU.

Exhibits and promotes a comprehensive understanding of the philanthropic priorities of the College, effectively matching the specific interests of prospects to those needs.

Plans for and initiates direct activities with prospects that are designed to enhance the affiliation between the prospect and FSU. Effectively communicates FSU’s mission and represents FSU’s culture to external stakeholders.

Central Development Collaboration

Coordinates with the Division of University Advancement colleagues to identify prospects for planned giving, corporate and foundation giving in partnership with the Office of University Research, and principal giving in partnership with the Principal Gifts Team. Protects confidential information. Perform other related duties as required and assigned.

Administrative/Events

Assists in the facilitation of meetings, communications, informational exchanges and project / philanthropic coordination with the faculty and faculty chairs. Prepares proposals and gift agreements as required for proper gift documentation. Prepares correspondence with prospects and documents communications, solicitation activity and gift information in compliance with the FSU Foundation’s reporting guidelines. Creates, inspires, and maintains donor loyalty, interest and enthusiasm through stewardship communication and activities designed to express recognition, appreciation and the impact of their gift(s). Implementation of such a stewardship plan may include but should not be limited to letters, communication of unit or university initiatives, invitations to appropriate activities, meetings, events, student engagement or the facilitation of campus visits.

Board/Volunteer Management

Assists in the management of all volunteer boards associated with the College of Medicine.

Qualifications

Master's degree and four years of experience in a related advancement field or a Bachelor's degree and six years of related experience. Higher education can substitute for experience at a comparable rate.

A valid Florida Driver's License or the ability to obtain upon hire.

University Information

One of the nation's elite research universities, Florida State University preserves, expands, and disseminates knowledge in the sciences, technology, arts, humanities, and professions, while embracing a philosophy of learning strongly rooted in the traditions of the liberal arts and critical thinking. Founded in 1851, Florida State University is the oldest continuous site of higher education in Florida. FSU is a community steeped in tradition that fosters research and encourages creativity. At FSU, there’s the excitement of being part of a vibrant academic and professional community, surrounded by people whose ideas are shaping tomorrow’s news!

new_jobs.description:
Vitamin Angels

Position Description

Position:
Director of Communications
Employer:
Vitamin Angels
Department:
Marketing & Communications
Location:
U.S. Remote
Salary Range:
 $130,000-170,000 
Every applicant is required to submit a cover letter with their application. 

About Vitamin Angels

Vitamin Angels is a global health organization working to save lives and improve the health of women and children most at risk through proven nutrition solutions. We prioritize high-impact, cost-effective, evidence-based nutrition interventions and apply evidence, implementation learning, and innovation to introduce, strengthen, and scale nutrition programs in geographies where we can achieve the greatest and most sustainable impact. Our programs are advanced through long-term partnerships that enable government and local partner ownership, are implemented within existing structures, and adapted to local contexts.
Vitamin Angels is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a supportive environment where all individuals have access to equal opportunities to succeed, regardless of background, identity, or perspective. Our efforts aim to ensure fairness and mutual respect for all employees, promoting a culture of belonging and professional growth.
Role or Purpose of Position

The Director of Communications is responsible for advancing Vitamin Angels’ visibility, credibility, reputation, and influence through strategic external and internal communications. The Director of Communications translates Vitamin Angels’ enterprise narrative into compelling communications that engage audiences, strengthen relationships, elevate organizational expertise, enhance credibility, position Vitamin Angels as a leading global health organization amongst diverse priority audiences, and build understanding and alignment across the organization.
As a senior communications leader, this role oversees corporate communications, media relations, executive communications, thought leadership, external editorial strategy, reputation management, crisis communications, and internal communications. The Director of Communications works closely with the VP of Marketing & Communications, various functional unit leads within Marketing and Communications, and technical and area experts throughout the organization to build Vitamin Angels recognition as a recognized industry thought leader and credible global health organization-of-choice.
The Director of Communications also partners closely with CEO, senior leadership team, People and Culture, and cross-functional teams to develop and deliver an effective internal communications strategy to unite the organization around common goals, systems, and strategies. 
Major Duties and Responsibilities

External Communications & Reputation
● Lead Vitamin Angels’ corporate communications, public and media relations, executive communications, and external communications editorial strategy—using the organization’s enterprise narrative, strategic priorities, and organizational voice—to strengthen visibility, credibility, and influence.
● Build, strengthen, and protect Vitamin Angels’ reputation among diverse priority audiences including current and prospective donors (corporate partners and foundations), technical stakeholders (global health community, other implementing organizations, multilaterals, etc.), and mass audiences.
● Develop and execute an integrated external communications strategy and program aligned with organizational priorities, strategic objectives, brand positioning, and fundraising goals, to amplify awareness and advocacy of Vitamin Angels.
● Develop proactive media strategies and compelling storylines that elevate Vitamin Angels’ expertise, evidence, impact, innovation, and leadership in global health and nutrition.
● Build and steward strategic relationships with priority media outlets, journalists, editors, global health and nutrition thought leaders, sector influencers, celebrities, and ambassadors, conveners, and relevant platforms.
● While Director of Partnership, in coordination with Directors of Digital Marketing and Brand, is responsible for owning the editorial calendar, this role is responsible for contributing to that calendar by way of communications activities and understanding how their function contributes to the success of the broader editorial calendar. 
Thought Leadership
● Serve as a strategic and trusted communications advisor to the VP Marketing & Communications, CEO, senior leadership team, and other organizational leaders, advising on messaging, positioning, and reputational opportunities/challenges.
● Partner with key stakeholders from across the organization, including local country team members, to identify communications opportunities and translate organizational priorities into effective communications strategies.
● Identify and train spokespeople and find/create opportunities for Vitamin Angels’ leaders and technical experts to contribute to important conversations through media, speaking engagements, opinion pieces, panels, conferences, podcasts, and other influential platforms. 
● Create a culture of thought leadership where key stakeholders (senior leadership team, technical experts, Board directors, etc.) understand the importance and value of looking for thought leadership opportunities and/or acting as thought leaders on behalf of Vitamin Angels. 
● Lead executive communications, including speeches, talking points, presentations, op-eds, interviews, leadership messaging, and other high-profile communications.
● Lead organizational strategy for events, convenings, and conferences, ensuring a comprehensive list of events for awareness and potential participation; ensuring that Vitamin Angels applies a right-fit level-of-effort for relevant gatherings.
Rapid Response & Crisis Communications 
● Monitor the external environment, emerging issues, media narratives, and reputational risks and advise leadership on communications opportunities and challenges.
● Lead crisis and issues communications strategy in coordination with the Senior Leadership Team, including Legal, and relevant functional leaders.
● Establish communications protocols, messaging frameworks, and rapid-response processes to ensure the organization is prepared to respond effectively to emerging issues.
Internal Communications & Organizational Alignment
● Lead Vitamin Angels’ internal communications strategy, ensuring employees are informed, connected, aligned, and engaged around the organization’s mission, strategy, priorities, and progress.
● Develop and manage the internal editorial calendar, communications channels, content strategy, and leadership communication cascades.
● Translate organizational strategy, priorities, decisions, milestones, and progress into clear, accessible, and meaningful communications that help employees understand how their work contributes to Vitamin Angels’ mission and impact.
● Define communications requirements for Vitamin Angels’ intranet or other employee communications platform and lead its content strategy, editorial governance, user experience, and adoption in partnership with Information Technology and People & Culture.
● Develop standards and governance for internal communications to promote consistency, clarity, accessibility, and effective information flow across the organization.
● Partner with the VP Marketing & Communications, CEO, People & Culture, and senior leadership team as needed to develop and execute change communications that help employees understand, navigate, and embrace organizational transformation.
● Equip leaders and managers with the messaging, tools, talking points, and communications resources needed to communicate consistently and effectively with their teams.
● Strengthen employee connection to Vitamin Angels’ mission, values, culture, strategy, and impact through purposeful storytelling and engagement.
● Establish mechanisms for gathering employee feedback and insights and use those inputs to improve internal communications and organizational alignment.
● Ensure internal communications complement and reinforce Vitamin Angels’ external narrative and organizational brand.
Team, Agency, & Resource Management
● Help build a culture in which communications is viewed as a strategic organizational function rather than solely a production or delivery service.
● Lead, mentor, and develop communications staff and external agency or freelance partners to build and maintain a high performing communications unit.
● Manage communications agencies, consultants, vendors, and other external partners to ensure high-quality, cost-effective delivery.
● Develop and manage communications budgets and resources in alignment with strategic priorities.
● Establish clear measures of communications effectiveness, using data and insights to optimize reach, engagement, reputation, and influence. While Directors of Brand Strategy and Digital and Partnership Marketing are responsible for tracking and analyzing their own-activities, this role is responsible for measuring distinct activities in communications and working with those Directors to understand how learnings can be applied to this role’s areas of responsibility, for continual improvement and a data-informed approach to start and stop activities.  

Level of Decision-Making

Within the bounds of Vitamin Angels’ mission, values and policies, and sound professional practices, the Director of Digital Marketing has the discretion to use independent judgment to make decisions of significant consequence that affect Vitamin Angels’ clients, partners, and employees.
Organizational Relationships

Vitamin Angels operates under a collaborative, matrix management model. The Director of Digital Marketing establishes their own daily work priorities and ensures that all responsibilities are conducted consistent with accepted best practices, sound professional judgment and within established schedule and budget.
Reports to:
VP, Marketing & Communications
Supervises:

· Technical Partner & Local Engagement
· Third party consultants/agency relationships
Primary working relationships:
· Director-level Marketing & Communications colleagues as a management team (SLT-1)
· Marketing Operations Manager
· Contacts from departments across the organization (Development, Programs, Finance and Administration, etc.)
Travel required:
International and domestic, as needed.

Qualifications and Skills (Required and Preferred)

● 15+ years of progressive experience in corporate communications, public relations, nonprofit communications, global health, international development, or a related field.

● Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, or a related field. 

● Experience working in a nonprofit, global health, international development, public health, or mission driven work is required. 

● Demonstrated experience developing and executing integrated communications strategies for complex organizations and diverse audiences.
● Strong track record in media relations, executive communications, thought leadership, reputation management, and issues/crisis communications.
● Experience communicating complex technical, scientific, health, or development topics in clear, compelling, and accessible ways.
● Demonstrated experience leading internal communications and organizational change communications.
● Exceptional writing, editing, storytelling, and verbal communication skills.
● Experience working with senior executives and subject-matter experts and translating their expertise into compelling external and internal communications.
● Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
● Experience managing teams, agencies, consultants, and budgets.
● Strong strategic judgment, political acumen, collaboration skills, and ability to operate with discretion and sound judgment.
